findings.title: Filter targets after, not before, template interpolation
findings.body: The code tests `query.expr` before calling `applyTemplateVariables`. A target whose expression is a template variable that resolves to an empty string therefore remains in `queries` and is subsequently classified, partitioned, and sent to Loki as an empty query. Empty expressions are normally intentionally skipped (as the existing `filter((query) => query.expr)` indicates). Interpolate first and then discard targets with an empty interpolated `expr`; the sharding entry point has the same ordering issue.

findings.title: Shard-split requests interpolate the same target repeatedly
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` applies template variables here, but every generated shard request is then passed to `runSplitQuery` at line 163, which now calls `applyTemplateVariables` again for every subrequest. This is not a harmless call-count increase: `applyTemplateVariables` also receives `request.filters`, so ad-hoc filters can be added repeatedly to the generated selector, and a template value containing another `$...` sequence can be interpreted on a later pass. The initial interpolation result should be treated as final when delegating to time splitting (or the lower-level split path should accept already-interpolated targets) rather than reapplying interpolation for each shard.

findings.title: Interpolated empty shard targets are executed instead of skipped
findings.body: The expression-presence filter runs before `applyTemplateVariables`. Consequently, a target such as an optional query variable that expands to an empty expression survives the filter and is passed into sharding and ultimately to `runSplitQuery`. This can issue invalid empty Loki queries instead of following the intended empty-query behavior. Apply interpolation before checking `query.expr` and remove targets whose interpolated expression is empty.
